translationRepairs: When Jing was pacified, Emperor Wen became administrator of Wu Commandery and made Zhongju deputy administrator; together with Yu Chi of Yingchuan he were both Emperor Wen's clients.
When Jing was pacified, Emperor Wen became administrator of Wu Commandery and made Zhongju deputy administrator; together with Yu Chi of Yingchuan they were both Emperor Wen's clients.
s0013 與潁川庾持俱為文帝賓客 makes Zhongju and Yu Chi joint clients; "he were" is ungrammatical for that plural subject, and "they were" restores agreement without changing meaning.
In the first year of Tiancheng (560) he was made acting minister of the masters of writing for officials and enfeoffed as Marquis of Bao’an with five hundred households.
In the first year of Tianjia (560) he was made acting minister of the masters of writing for officials and enfeoffed as Marquis of Bao’an with five hundred households.
s0016 opens with 天嘉元年; the Chen reign name is Tianjia, not Tiancheng, and the proposed sentence otherwise matches the offices, fief, and AD 560 conversion.
In the first year of Tiancheng, he was made acting Minister of the Masters of Writing for Officials, enfeoffed Marquis of Bao'an county with a fief of five hundred households.
In the first year of Tianjia, he was made acting Minister of the Masters of Writing for Officials, enfeoffed Marquis of Bao'an county with a fief of five hundred households.
The same unit’s literal field also renders 天嘉 as Tiancheng; replacing it with Tianjia corrects the reign name while leaving the rest of the literal wording intact.

Earlier Zhongju’s son Yu had married Emperor Wen’s sister, Princess Xin’an the Long of Xinyi. He rose to attendant gentleman of the secretariat, then went out as administrator of Xuancheng, and Emperor Wen gave him troops and horses. That year he was named interior minister of Nankang but had not yet taken office because of the state mourning.

Earlier Zhongju’s son Yu had married Emperor Wen’s sister, the Senior Princess of Xinyi. He rose to attendant gentleman of the secretariat, then went out as administrator of Xuancheng, and Emperor Wen gave him troops and horses. That year he was named interior minister of Nankang but had not yet taken office because of the state mourning.
s0028 信義長公主 is the Senior Princess of Xinyi; "Princess Xin’an the Long of Xinyi" misreads 長公主 and invents Xin’an, while the proposed title matches the Chinese.
When the Founder campaigned against Zhang Biao, Shen Tai and others had already surrendered. The Founder held the prefectural city, and Zhou Wenyü garrisoned north of the city at Xiang
When Emperor Wen campaigned against Zhang Biao, Shen Tai and others had already surrendered. Emperor Wen held the prefectural city, and Zhou Wenyü garrisoned north of the city at Xiang
s0058 twice names 文帝 as the campaigner and holder of the prefectural city; "the Founder" (高祖) is the wrong person, and Emperor Wen restores the source referent.
When the Founder campaigned against Zhang Biao, Shen Tai and others had already surrendered; the Founder held the prefectural city, and Zhou Wenyü garrisoned north of the city at Xiang
When Emperor Wen campaigned against Zhang Biao, Shen Tai and others had already surrendered; Emperor Wen held the prefectural city, and Zhou Wenyü garrisoned north of the city at Xiang
The literal of s0058 likewise substitutes Founder for 文帝; replacing both occurrences with Emperor Wen matches the Chinese agents.

[1] Zhang Biao returned by night from Shan county to storm the city. The Founder slipped out the north gate. In the sudden dark the troops panicked. Wenyü did not know where the Founder was—only Zigao stood beside him. The Founder sent Zigao through the chaos to Wenyü, bring back his orders, then go again in the dark to steady the army.

[1] Zhang Biao returned by night from Shan county to storm the city. Emperor Wen slipped out the north gate. In the sudden dark the troops panicked. Wenyü did not know where Emperor Wen was—only Zigao stood beside him. Emperor Wen sent Zigao through the chaos to Wenyü to bring back his orders, then go again in the dark to steady the army.
s0061 repeatedly has 文帝, so Founder is wrong; the proposed Emperor Wen swaps are right, but "to Wenyü, bring back" remains ungrammatical, so the infinitive needs "to bring back".

Zhang Biao returned by night from Shan county to raid the city. The Founder went out through the northern gate. In the sudden rush of dark evening the soldiers were in turmoil; Wenyü too had not yet determined where the Founder was—only Zigao was at his side. The Founder then sent Zigao from amid the disorderly troops to go see Wenyü, return with orders and replies, and in the dark go again to comfort the armies.

Zhang Biao returned by night from Shan county to raid the city. Emperor Wen went out through the northern gate. In the sudden rush of dark evening the soldiers were in turmoil; Wenyü too had not yet determined where Emperor Wen was—only Zigao was at his side. Emperor Wen then sent Zigao from amid the disorderly troops to go see Wenyü, return with orders and replies, and in the dark go again to comfort the armies.
s0061’s literal likewise calls 文帝 the Founder three times; Emperor Wen correctly restores the named actor in each slot.
The Founder’s scattered men slowly gathered. Zigao led him into Wenyü’s camp and together they threw up palisades.
Emperor Wen’s scattered men slowly gathered. Zigao led him into Wenyü’s camp and together they threw up palisades.
s0062 文帝散兵稍集 attributes the scattered troops to Emperor Wen; Founder is a false referent and the proposed wording is otherwise sound.
The Founder's scattered troops gradually gathered; Zigao led him into Wenyü's camp, and together they built palisades.
Emperor Wen's scattered troops gradually gathered; Zigao led him into Wenyü's camp, and together they built palisades.
The literal of s0062 makes the same Founder error for 文帝; Emperor Wen is the correct owner of the scattered troops.
The Founder then gave Zigao many of his own followers. Zigao was generous and courteous to officers, and men flocked to him.
Emperor Wen then gave Zigao many of his own followers. Zigao was generous and courteous to officers, and men flocked to him.
s0064 文帝乃分憤下多配子高 has Emperor Wen assigning followers; Founder misidentifies the giver.
The Founder then assigned many of his subordinates to Zigao; Zigao also was generous with wealth and courteous to officers; those who came to him were very numerous.
Emperor Wen then assigned many of his subordinates to Zigao; Zigao also was generous with wealth and courteous to officers; those who came to him were very numerous.
The literal likewise needs Emperor Wen for 文帝 as the one who redistributes subordinates to Zigao.
Xiao Kui made Jiao minister of works and set Dai Sengshuo over Ba, Ren Mannu over Hengyang, Pan Zhizhen over Baling, and Zhang Zhaoyu over Yueyang;
Xiao Kui made Jiao minister of works and set Dai Sengshuo over Ba, Ren Mannu over Hengyang, Pan Zhiquan over Baling, and Zhang Zhaoyu over Yueyang;
s0119 names 潘智虔; 8654 is quan (qián), so Zhiquan is correct and Zhizhen invents a different given name.

Xiao Kui appointed Jiao Minister of Works; Dai Sengshuo, Administrator of Ba; Ren Mannu, Interior Minister of Hengyang; Pan Zhizhen, Interior Minister of Baling; Zhang Zhaoyu, Administrator of Yueyang;

Xiao Kui appointed Jiao Minister of Works; Dai Sengshuo, Administrator of Ba; Ren Mannu, Interior Minister of Hengyang; Pan Zhiquan, Interior Minister of Baling; Zhang Zhaoyu, Administrator of Yueyang;
The same personal name 潘智虔 appears in the literal field; Pan Zhiquan matches the characters and Zhizhen does not.

Jiao early took part in intimate service, [8] once shared in hardship and peril, knew that he had no concealment, and was rewarded with full exertion; there was the sincerity of one trusted, not ground for suspicion.

Jiao early took part in intimate service, [8] once shared in hardship and peril; [the emperor] knew that he had nothing to hide and rewarded him for exerting his full strength—there was the sincerity of one trusted, not ground for suspicion.
Following s0162's Emperor Wen as subject, s0163 知其無隱、賞以悉力 means the emperor knew Jiao had nothing to hide and rewarded his full effort; the proposed literal restores agent and sense.
